Aircraft provide aerial cover and vital support for your ground forces. They range from nimble jet fighters to specialized electronic warfare aircraft.

#cyan{Air Defense} aircraft aim to establish air superiority. #cyan{Support} and #cyan{Anti-Tank} aircraft are used to destroy enemy land units, either as Close Air Support (CAS) or bombers. #cyan{SEAD} (Suppression of Enemy Air Defense) planes are designed to neutralize enemy air defense systems. Many aircraft are multirole, with different weapon payloads for specific combat missions.
This category groups all units within the Armory.
Artillery has been called "The King of the Battlefield" for good reason. From mortars to self-propelled howitzers, artillery can rain destructive fire down on targets far away.

#cyan{Artillery} units, such as howitzers and mortars, provide indirect fire and smoke screens over long ranges. They can be towed or self-propelled for additional battlefield mobility. Available in various calibers, which determines their range and firepower, artillery also includes multiple launch rocket systems (MLRS).
Anti-Aircraft (AA) guns are designed to take out low-flying airborne targets. They are frequently emplaced in dual or even quadruple quick-traversing mounts with high rates of fire and elevation.
#cyan{Air Defense} units use surface-to-air missiles or rapid-firing anti-air guns to neutralize enemy aircraft and helicopters.

This category groups all types of #cyan{defensive infrastructure} such as #cyan{barbed wire}, #cyan{trenches}, #cyan{gun pits} & #cyan{bunkers}.

- #cyan{Barbed wire} can be stretched in lines over the map, and will slow down any units (yes, even tanks!), friends or foe, passing through.
- #cyan{Trenches} can also be stretched over the map, and will allow #cyan{infantry squads}, #cyan{heavy machine-guns} & #cyan{anti-tank teams} to benefit from heavy cover similar to that of a building.
- #cyan{Gun pits} are single positions which can't be extended as trenches, yet they provide the same level of cover for larger #cyan{artillery}, #cyan{anti-aircraft} and #cyan{anti-tank} guns. A gun in a gun pit may fire at 360°.
- #cyan{Bunkers} come in two types: #cyan{machine gun bunkers} & #cyan{anti-tank bunkers}. The former can only engage unarmored targets and vehicles, while the latter only engages vehicles. AT bunker comes in different calibers, from small #cyan{anti-tank rifles} to medium #cyan{anti-tank guns}. All bunker have a #cyan{restricted field of view} which can be seen and modified when placing the bunker.

All defensive infrastructure can only be deployed in the #cyan{deployment phase}. Once the game is launched, you are unable to deploy any defenses.
The boots on the ground of your Battlegroup. While slow on foot and fragile in the open, infantry excels in attacking and holding terrain.

Infantry units come in a variety of shapes and sizes, with different levels of training and manpower, as well as Traits and weaponry. They perform a variety of roles, from general #cyan{infantry squads} to close-combat #cyan{assault squads} and #cyan{command squads} who can capture zones and improve friendly troops near them. Smaller weapon teams are built around crew-served weapons including #cyan{support} and #cyan{anti-tank}. #cyan{Forward Deployed} units can deploy much further than regular units at the start of a battle.

The supply chain keeps your Battlegroup in top fighting condition, while command units improve nearby troops and let you capture Command Zones. Both types of units are crucial in achieving victory on the battlefield.

#cyan{Supply} vehicles replenish ammo and fuel, and can repair other units in the field, including infantry squads. #cyan{Forward Operating Bases} are fixed structures that can only be deployed at the start of a battle. They contain a large quantity of supplies. #cyan{Command} units are crucial in capturing zones and improving the performance of nearby units.
Tanks are the muscles of your Battlegroup. Main battle tanks spearhead the offensive, supported by a variety of other armored vehicles.

#cyan{Tanks} come in various shapes and sizes, with a focus on armor, firepower, mobility, or designed for a more balanced approach. Advances in technology has divided the main battle tank into various generations. #cyan{Armored Personnel Carriers} transport infantry on the battlefield, as do #cyan{Infantry Fighting Vehicles} which usually feature heavier armor and armaments. Dedicated #cyan{Anti-Tank} units include towed guns and long-range ATGM carriers. #cyan{Command} vehicles boost nearby units and lets you capture Command Zones.

Helicopters fly nap of the earth. They use speed and agility to perform a variety of combat missions at low altitudes.

#cyan{Transport} helicopters can quickly move units across the battlefield. #cyan{Support} rotorcraft excel in attacking enemy ground units with machine guns, autocannons or rockets. #cyan{Anti-Tank} helicopters are sometimes fitted with armor, ECM and are designed specifically to engage enemy armor with guided missiles and heavy weaponry.
The eyes and ears of your Battlegroup. Recon units scout the battlefield and provide critical intel on enemy targets.

Reconnaissance units are varied. They can be two-man sniper teams, special forces squads, unarmed fast vehicles, nimble helicopters or specialized units with ground surveillance radars. Recon units depend on #cyan{Stealth} and #cyan{Optics}, and at times speed, to observe the enemy while remaining hidden. Reconnaissance units can #cyan{deploy ahead} of the main force during the Deployment Phase.
